claims.text: The initial material is an as-cast HfMoTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy.
Approximately 5 at.% Cr will replace Hf in HfMoTaTiZr.
The Cr-modified alloy will be synthesized by vacuum arc melting.
Adding approximately 5 at.% Cr will reduce the density of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Adding approximately 5 at.% Cr will retain the room-temperature and high-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Cr addition is expected to produce a Cr-containing solid-solution phase.
The Cr-containing solid solution is expected to preserve phase connectivity and other microstructural features that support mechanical performance.
Chromium has a lower atomic mass than hafnium.
Replacing Hf with Cr should lower alloy density by reducing average atomic mass.
Cr can contribute solid-solution strengthening in the modified HfMoTaTiZr alloy.
Cr is chemically compatible enough to enter the HfMoTaTiZr microstructure without severely disrupting its balance of mechanical properties.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline density is approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline room-temperature yield strength is approximately 1600 MPa.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline yield strength at 1000 °C is approximately 855 MPa.
The baseline is characterized as having good room-temperature ductility exceeding 50%.
The modified alloy is predicted to reduce density by at least 5% relative to 10.21 g/cm³.
The modified alloy is predicted to retain yield strengths near 1600 MPa at room temperature and 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
The modified alloy is predicted to retain ductility comparable to the baseline, with no significant reduction.
Mechanical properties will be compared at room temperature and 1000 °C under tensile or compressive loading.
The hypothesis is rejected if density reduction is below 5%, or if yield strength at either test temperature or ductility decreases by more than approximately 10% relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: The baseline assigns good room-temperature ductility above 50% to the HfMoTaTiZr comparison, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that effects on ductility remain uncertain; moreover, the stated >50% value is described as coming from related alloys rather than the named baseline itself.
